chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from someone who narrated it, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Concerning a man who died and entrusted matters to a man while he had a young son. When the boy came of age, he went to the executor and said to him, “Return my wealth to me so that I may marry,” but he refused him, so he went away until he committed zina.
He عليه السلام said: “Two-thirds of the sin of this man’s zina is borne by that executor who withheld the wealth from him and did not give it to him, by which he could have married.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: the executor or trustee appointed over the deceased’s affairs
key_terms.زَنَى: he committed zina, unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.مَالِي: my wealth or property rightfully belonging to me
key_terms.مَنَعَهُ: he prevented or withheld from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an executor who withholds an heir’s wealth until it leads him into zina?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when an executor wrongfully withholds the matured heir’s property, causing him to be unable to marry and fall into zina, the executor bears a major share of the sin. It emphasizes the legal and moral gravity of denying people their rightful wealth, especially when that denial leads to serious wrongdoing.
